questions.question_text: For which value of $m$ does $x^{2}-8x+2m=0$ have equal roots?

options.why: Solved $64-2m=0$, forgetting the factor of $4$ in $4ac=8m$.
Made a sign error when solving $-8m=-64$, yielding $m=-8$.
Used $b=8$ and calculated $\Delta=64-4m=0$ instead of $4ac=8m$.

questions.question_text: For which values of $k$ does $x^{2}+6x+(k+2)=0$ have two distinct real roots?

options.why: Reached $-4k>-28$ correctly but divided by $-4$ without reversing the inequality symbol.
Did not distribute the $-4$ over the constant $2$, solving $36-4k>0$ and so $-4k>-36$.
Failed to distribute the $-4$ over the $2$ AND divided $-4k>-36$ by $-4$ without reversing the symbol.

questions.question_text: For which values of $p$ does $3x^{2}-6x+p=0$ have no real roots?

options.why: Reached $-12p<-36$ correctly but divided by $-12$ without reversing the inequality symbol.
Left the coefficient $a=3$ out of $4ac$, solving $36-4p<0$ and so $-4p<-36$.
Omitted $a=3$ from $4ac$ AND divided $-4p<-36$ by $-4$ without reversing the symbol.

questions.question_text: For which values of $k$ does $x^{2}-6x+2k=0$ have two distinct real roots?

options.why: Reached $-8k>-36$ correctly but divided by $-8$ without reversing the inequality symbol.
Evaluated $(-6)^{2}$ as $-36$, giving $\Delta=-36-8k$ and solving $-8k>36$.
Used $\Delta\ge0$, including $k=\frac{9}{2}$ where the roots are equal.

questions.question_text: For which values of $k$ does $x^{2}+kx+64=0$ have equal roots?

options.why: Found only the positive root and overlooked the negative root $k=-16$.
Took the square root of $64$ directly instead of solving $k^2-4(64)=0$.
Reached $k^2=256$ but did not take the square root, and incorrectly attached $\pm$ to the unsquared value $256$.

questions.question_text: For which values of $m$ does $x^{2}+mx+9=0$ have two distinct real roots?

options.why: Gave the region between the roots where $\Delta<0$ instead of the outside region where $\Delta>0$.
Omitted the negative interval $m<-6$, which also satisfies $m^2>36$.
Used non-strict inequalities, including the boundary values where roots are equal.

questions.question_text: For which value of $k$ does $x^{2}+5x+2k=0$ have equal roots?

options.why: Omitted the factor $2$ in the constant coefficient, solving $25-4k=0$.
Made a sign error when dividing $-8k=-25$ by $-8$.
Omitted the factor $4$ in $4ac$, solving $25-2k=0$.

questions.question_text: For which values of $k$ does $2x^{2}+kx+8=0$ have no real roots?

options.why: Gave the outside region where $\Delta>0$ instead of the inside region where $\Delta<0$.
Incorrectly used $2ac$ instead of $4ac$ and also omitted $a=2$, giving $2(1)(8)=16$ and solving $k^2-16<0$.
Used non-strict inequalities, including $k=\pm8$ which gives equal real roots rather than no real roots.

questions.question_text: For which value of $p>0$ does $px^{2}+2(p+2)x+(p+5)=0$ have equal roots?

options.why: Made a sign error when solving $4(4-p)=0$, obtaining $p=-4$.
Set the constant term $p+5=0$ instead of the discriminant, then made a sign error by reporting $p=5$ rather than $p=-5$.
Set $p+2=0$ from the linear coefficient instead of evaluating the discriminant, then made a sign error by reporting $p=2$ rather than $p=-2$.
